title: Separable perturbation and factor selection
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], let $K(t)$ carry a valuation subring $O$ with $R=O\cap K$, and suppose $f\in K[T]$ is monic irreducible and $f(t)/\pi\in O^\times$ has transcendental residue over $\kappa(R)$ for some $\pi\in K^\times$. Then there is a monic separable irreducible polynomial $g\in K[T]$ and $\pi'\in K^\times$ such that $g(t)/\pi'\in O^\times$ and its residue is transcendental over $\kappa(R)$. Since $K$ is separably closed, every monic separable irreducible $g\in K[T]$ has degree one. Here $K$ is a field [def-weil-field], $K[T]$ is the polynomial ring in one indeterminate [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and a valuation subring $B$ of a field $F$ is a subring with $x\in B$ or $x^{-1}\in B$ for every $x\ne0$; $\mathfrak m_B=B\setminus B^\times$ and $\kappa(B)=B/\mathfrak m_B$. The field and transcendence conventions are [def-pc-field-extension, def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Here $K(t)$ is the fraction field of $K[t]$ [def-weil-rational-function-field], and separable means coprime to the formal derivative [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. Monic means leading coefficient $1$; irreducible means nonzero, not a unit, and with a unit factor in every factorization in $K[T]$.

proof.text: Put $L=K(t)$, $k=\kappa(R)$, $l=\kappa(O)$, and $u=f(t)/\pi$. The restriction of the quotient map embeds $k$ in $l$: for $b\in K^\times$, $b\in R^\times$ if and only if $b,b^{-1}\in O$, if and only if $b\in O^\times$, so $\mathfrak m_R=K\cap\mathfrak m_O$. By [def-weil-rational-function-field], $L$ is generated as a field by $t$, and $t$ is transcendental: a nonzero polynomial stays nonzero in its fraction field. Thus $\{t\}$ is a transcendence basis (the extension over the field it generates is the identity), and [def-kun-transcendence-degree] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=1$. The transcendental residue $\bar u$ gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k l\ge1$. Apply [lem-trf-abhyankar-inequality] to the finitely generated field extension $K\subset L$ and $O$. Since its rational-rank summand is nonnegative, it gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k l\le1$. Hence $\operatorname{trdeg}_k l=1$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-residual-curve-value-group] with $L=K(t)$ and the residue transcendence degree just proved. It gives, for every $y\in L^\times$, a $c_y\in K^\times$ with $y/c_y\in O^\times$. In particular choose $c\in K^\times$ such that $x=t/c$ is a unit. We will also apply exactly this same conclusion to each $t-a_i\ne0$; nonvanishing follows because $t$ is transcendental.

proof.text: First suppose $R=K$. Every nonzero constant, including $c$ and $\pi$, is then a unit of $O$, and $t=cx$ is a unit. If its residue $\tau$ were algebraic over $K=k$, then $f(\tau)/\pi$ would be algebraic over $K$: [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure] explicitly says that algebraic elements form a subfield containing the base. But $f(\tau)/\pi=\bar u$ is transcendental, a contradiction. Thus $g(T)=T$ and $\pi'=1$ have the required residue. The polynomial $T$ is monic and irreducible (a nonconstant factor of a degree-one polynomial has constant complementary factor, which is a unit), and is separable because its derivative is $1$. We may henceforth assume $R\ne K$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof p. 28, separable perturbation paragraph; expanded for the item’s unrestricted t and trivial restriction valuation. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: If $f$ is already separable, take $g=f$ and $\pi'=\pi$; all the required residue conditions are the hypotheses. Otherwise [lem-trf-irreducible-separable-derivative] gives $f'=0$. Since $f$ is monic and nonconstant, its degree $d$ is positive. It cannot have degree one, since the derivative of a monic linear polynomial is $1$. Thus $d\ge2$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-separable-polynomial-linear-factorization], write $h(T)=\prod_{i=1}^n(T-a_i)$ with $a_i\in K$. Since $h$ has positive degree the list is nonempty. For every $i$, $t-a_i\ne0$, so [lem-trf-residual-curve-value-group] gives $c_i\in K^\times$ such that $v_i=(t-a_i)/c_i\in O^\times$. Put $C=\prod_i c_i$. Evaluating the factorization and dividing by $\pi$ gives $h(t)/\pi=(C/\pi)\prod_i v_i$. The left side and all $v_i$ are units of $O$, hence $C/\pi\in K\cap O^\times=R^\times$. Reduction therefore gives $\bar u=\overline{C/\pi}\prod_i\bar v_i$ in $l$, with $\overline{C/\pi}\in k^\times$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof p. 28, separable perturbation paragraph; expanded for the item’s unrestricted t and trivial restriction valuation. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: If every $\bar v_i$ were algebraic over $k$, their product, and its product with $\overline{C/\pi}\in k^\times$, would be algebraic over $k$: use the subfield and multiplication clauses stated in [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure], iterated over the finite list. This contradicts the transcendence of $\bar u$. Choose an index $j$ with $\bar v_j$ transcendental. Then $g(T)=T-a_j$ and $\pi'=c_j$ have the required unit and residue properties. The linear polynomial is monic, irreducible by the degree argument of Step 3, and separable by the Bezout identity $0\cdot g+1\cdot g'=1$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof p. 28, separable perturbation paragraph; expanded for the item’s unrestricted t and trivial restriction valuation. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Finally let $g$ be any monic separable irreducible polynomial over $K$. Apply [lem-trf-separable-polynomial-linear-factorization] to $g$. Its factor list cannot be empty, since then $g=1$ is a unit. If there were at least two factors, splitting off the first would factor $g$ into two monic polynomials of positive degree, neither a unit, contradicting irreducibility. Thus there is exactly one factor and $\deg g=1$. This also covers the already-separable branch of Step 4.
